scope.purpose: Check the five selected crafting values using the hosted browser, preserve new evidence, and update draft evidence notes without changing the loadout or publishing.

method.surface: Hosted Chrome browser; direct DDO Wiki page DOM inspection.
method.capture_kind: Scoped rendered-text and tooltip-HTML extractions, not complete raw HTTP responses, screenshots, or independent in-game observations.
method.observation_clock: Each body_observation interval is bounded by clock__curr_time results immediately before and after the new DOM extraction. These are new access windows, not the original historical capture dates, page modification dates, or later receipt-creation times.
method.revision_limit: revision_link is the Permanent link exposed by the page read; it identifies the displayed page revision. The permanent-link URL was not independently loaded again.
method.source_authority: DDO Wiki is a community-maintained secondary source. Direct Wiki support does not by itself certify all live-game interactions.
method.attribution: DDO Wiki contributors, identified through each article and revision link.

nearly_complete.upgrade_rule_visible_text: Which set of enchantments is available for an item depends on which version of the Nearly Complete enchantment the item has. For example, an item with Nearly Complete: Ability Score can be upgraded with an Enhancement bonus to one of the core stats. Upgrading an item with Nearly Completed requires 25 Abyssal Gems (or Legendary Abyssal Gems for Legendary items) from Terror of Demogorgon end chests. Note that you cannot replace a Nearly Completed upgrade after selecting one - you will need a new copy of the item to apply a different effect. Play Tabletop RPGs
nearly_complete.extraction_note: The trailing 'Play Tabletop RPGs' was present in the extracted paragraph and is retained verbatim; it is not treated as a crafting rule.
nearly_complete.crafting_location_visible_text: Nearly Completed is a crafting mechanic that allows players to upgrade items from the Terror of Demogorgon expansion with an extra enchantment from a small list at the Duergar Completion Forge in Gravenhollow.

slave_lords.gem_slot_rule_visible_text: The next step is to speak to a barter NPC to exchange the basic ingredients for "gems" of different sorts (see below), which will be used to give you the effects on your items. Each of the 3 common and 3 uncommon ingredients allows a different kind of effect on the item, and there are 6 possible to create for each item you will create - prefix, suffix, bonus, extra, augment slot (clear, yellow, blue, or green), and set bonus (your choice of 3 possible). Tables below show what sort of effects can go into each of these.
slave_lords.locked_effect_rule_visible_text: The last step is to use those gems on the item itself to create the effects you want - and your item is complete! If you don't have all the ingredients you want now, you can always upgrade it later, but you cannot "erase" or change an effect - once it's there, it's locked in.

fortification.standard_item_rule_visible_text: Items are the primary source of fortification for most player characters. Standard fortification items provide enhancement bonuses to fortification. Multiple effects do not stack with each other. You can combine them with rarer Insightful Fortification items (insight bonus). Item effects fully stack with the racial fortification, enhancements, or epic destiny perks.
fortification.scope_limit: General item classification, not a finished Legendary Chains tooltip. No new pairwise stacking edge is approved from this paragraph.

findings.conclusion: The Legendary Prefix recipe explicitly lists +142% Fortification. Enhancement is supported by the general standard-item rule, not an exact completed Chains tooltip. This is not the unselected Quality Fortification +35% Bonus craft.
findings.remaining: Exact finished-effect bonus-type binding and component integration remain open; no Queen-plus-Chains Fortification total is certified.

findings.conclusion: The Legendary Suffix recipe supplies +142 single-type Equipment Spell Power; the Spell Power table maps Combustion to Fire. This is a cross-page mapping, not a fabricated single +142 Combustion tooltip.
findings.remaining: Component integration must preserve the actual source wording and explicitly handle the Combustion/Fire Spell Power mapping. Fire-imbue applicability remains separate. This is not 142 weapon damage or measured ranged DPS.

findings.conclusion: The Legendary Bonus recipe lists Quality Attributes +3. Applying that attribute category to the selected Intelligence craft is an explicit mapping, not a captured finished-item Intelligence tooltip.
findings.remaining: Selected-attribute applicability binding and component integration remain open; no complete Intelligence or damage total is certified.

findings.conclusion: The Legendary Extra recipe lists Skills (except UMD) +20, supporting the selected Spot magnitude by category mapping. The retained recipe does not explicitly name the bonus type; Competence remains the selected model assumption, not a newly verified claim.
findings.remaining: Obtain an exact finished-effect or equivalent authoritative type statement for this craft, then integrate its source bindings and independently validate its interactions. The recipe alone does not certify the direct Spot subtotal or final Wisdom-based Spot score.

construction_findings: Legendary Chains may be worn at Waist, so it does not conflict with the selected neck pendant.
The four selected effects use separate Prefix, Suffix, Extra and Bonus channels. The Green augment slot is a separate unlock, not inherent on the uncrafted host.
Nearly Complete upgrades cannot be replaced on the same item under the observed rule; Slave Lords effects are likewise described as locked after application.
No crafting was performed, no materials spent, no ownership or current acquisition stock assumed, and no optional Mythic or Slave Lords set bonus added.
